scenes.visual: Same COLOUR MAP (used in both films): 16:9, warm off-white background, flat cartoon style, no molecular structures. Paramecium = TEAL slipper-shaped cell with a fringe of short hairs (cilia). Food = AMBER dots (bacteria). Oxygen = CYAN dots; carbon dioxide = GREY dots. Water = PALE BLUE droplets. Wastes = BROWN specks. The JOB CHECKLIST is a white panel on the right with six icons in this order, each with a grey tick box: a running arrow 'move', a fork 'get food', two arrows in and out 'gas exchange', a bin with a droplet 'get rid of wastes and water', a lightning bolt 'respond', a cell splitting in two 'reproduce'. The FIVE LEVELS have fixed colours: cell = PURPLE, tissue = BLUE, organ = GREEN, organ system = ORANGE, organism = GOLD. Red blood cell = RED disc dented on both faces. Anything not computed from the lesson's numbers carries a small corner label 'schematic'. A LEVEL STRIP runs up the left side: five empty boxes from bottom to top, outlined in PURPLE, BLUE, GREEN, ORANGE and GOLD, still unlabelled. Title card 'One Job, Five Levels' fades in.

scenes.tts: The first film ended with many small cells sharing the job list. So who gets oxygen to the cells in your toes, far from your lungs? Those toe cells need it right now.
scenes.visual: The cluster of small cells from the first film shrinks into a cartoon student outline. A CYAN oxygen dot sits at the lungs; a pulsing ring marks the toes. A dotted question-mark path joins them.
scenes.narration: The first film ended with many small cells sharing the job list. So who gets oxygen to the cells in your toes, far from your lungs? Those toe cells need it right now.

scenes.tts: Follow that one job. It starts with one kind of cell. A red blood cell is a small, flexible disc, dented on both sides. It carries oxygen.
scenes.visual: Zoom to a RED disc, shown face-on and then side-on to reveal the dent on both faces. CYAN dots load onto it. The bottom box of the level strip fills PURPLE and gets the label 'cell'.
scenes.narration: Follow that one job. It starts with one kind of cell. A red blood cell is a small, flexible disc, dented on both sides. It carries oxygen.

scenes.tts: A cell whose shape and parts suit it to one kind of job is called a specialized cell. In mammals, including humans, a mature red blood cell has no nucleus.
scenes.visual: Label 'specialized cell' attaches to the RED disc. A ghost outline of a nucleus fades out of its centre; label 'no nucleus when mature'.
scenes.narration: A cell whose shape and parts suit it to one kind of job is called a specialized cell. In mammals, including humans, a mature red blood cell has no nucleus.

scenes.tts: Here is a blood vessel narrower than the red blood cell. What would let the cell get through? Pause and decide.
scenes.visual: A pink tube narrows ahead of the RED disc to a gap clearly smaller than the disc's width. The disc stops at the opening. 'Pause and predict' appears.
scenes.narration: Here is a blood vessel narrower than the red blood cell. What would let the cell get through? Pause and decide.

scenes.visual: Hold on the RED disc at the narrow opening; a countdown bar shrinks along the bottom.

scenes.tts: Its shape. The flexible disc bends and folds, squeezes through the very narrow vessel, and springs back on the other side.
scenes.visual: The RED disc folds like a soft taco, slides through the narrow tube, and springs back to a disc beyond it, still carrying its CYAN dots.
scenes.narration: Its shape. The flexible disc bends and folds, squeezes through the very narrow vessel, and springs back on the other side.

scenes.tts: But blood has to be pushed. That job belongs to heart muscle cells. Each one is striped, and it shortens to squeeze.
scenes.visual: A short, branching, striped PURPLE-outlined heart muscle cell appears beside the vessel. It shortens and relaxes in a slow rhythm, label 'heart muscle cell: shortens'.
scenes.narration: But blood has to be pushed. That job belongs to heart muscle cells. Each one is striped, and it shortens to squeeze.

scenes.tts: Many heart muscle cells link up into a network. Similar cells doing one job form a tissue. This one is heart muscle tissue, and its cells shorten together.
scenes.visual: Copies of the striped cell, short and branching, slide in and link end to end into a connected network that shortens together (schematic). The second box of the level strip fills BLUE, label 'tissue: similar cells, one job'.
scenes.narration: Many heart muscle cells link up into a network. Similar cells doing one job form a tissue. This one is heart muscle tissue, and its cells shorten together.

scenes.tts: Heart muscle tissue works together with other kinds of tissue. Different tissues working together form an organ, the heart.
scenes.visual: The BLUE heart-muscle network sits in place beside two other differently patterned tissues (schematic); together they are shown filling a cartoon heart that beats. No curling or wrapping. The third box fills GREEN, label 'organ: different tissues'.
scenes.narration: Heart muscle tissue works together with other kinds of tissue. Different tissues working together form an organ, the heart.

scenes.tts: The heart pushes blood, fresh from the lungs, through a branching set of blood vessels. Organs working together form an organ system. The heart and blood vessels are one.
scenes.visual: Branching vessels grow out from the heart through a body outline; RED discs flow along them. The fourth box fills ORANGE, label 'organ system: heart and blood vessels'.
scenes.narration: The heart pushes blood, fresh from the lungs, through a branching set of blood vessels. Organs working together form an organ system. The heart and blood vessels are one.

scenes.tts: All the systems together make the organism, you. Now the oxygen reaches the cells in your toes. That one job took every level, from one cell to the whole body.
scenes.visual: The full student outline appears around the system. RED discs arrive at the toes and CYAN dots pass into the small cells there. The top box fills GOLD, label 'organism'.
scenes.narration: All the systems together make the organism, you. Now the oxygen reaches the cells in your toes. That one job took every level, from one cell to the whole body.

scenes.tts: Other cells have other shapes for other jobs. A nerve cell has long branches. It carries signals over long distances, in some cases about a metre.
scenes.visual: A nerve cell with a long branch stretches from the spine down the leg toward the foot; a bright pulse travels along it. On screen: 'in some cases about 1 metre'.
scenes.narration: Other cells have other shapes for other jobs. A nerve cell has long branches. It carries signals over long distances, in some cases about a metre.

scenes.tts: A muscle cell in your arm is long and thin. It shortens to pull on bones. Three cells, three shapes, each fitting its job.
scenes.visual: A long thin arm muscle cell shortens and the forearm bone lifts. Then the RED disc, the nerve cell and the arm muscle cell line up side by side (not to scale), each tagged with its job: 'carries oxygen', 'carries signals', 'shortens to pull'.
scenes.narration: A muscle cell in your arm is long and thin. It shortens to pull on bones. Three cells, three shapes, each fitting its job.

scenes.tts: Now zoom back down the levels. That heart muscle cell is still a cell. But it sits inside every level above it: a tissue, the heart, the circulatory system and you.
scenes.visual: The camera zooms from the whole student down the level strip, GOLD to ORANGE to GREEN to BLUE to PURPLE, ending on one striped heart muscle cell. Each box flashes as the camera passes it.
scenes.narration: Now zoom back down the levels. That heart muscle cell is still a cell. But it sits inside every level above it: a tissue, the heart, the circulatory system and you.

scenes.tts: Sharing the work like this is division of labor. Each level does part of the job, and the levels depend on each other.
scenes.visual: All five boxes of the level strip glow together, linked by arrows from bottom to top: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism. Banner 'division of labor'.
scenes.narration: Sharing the work like this is division of labor. Each level does part of the job, and the levels depend on each other.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot beside the five-colour level strip. Take-home line: 'Cells shaped for their jobs build tissues, organs, systems and you.'
